why: QStream is a named branded online learning platform implementing spaced retrieval practice, not a general learning theory.
name: QStream
product_description: QStream is an online spaced-education platform developed by Harvard Medical School that delivers case-based questions, repeated retrieval, and corrective feedback at scheduled intervals for professional learners.

why: QSim is a named prototype simulation software tool rather than a general instructional element.
name: QSim
product_description: QSim is a prototype quantum-dynamics simulation developed by C. Savage and colleagues that visualizes wavefunction evolution and position measurements for teaching introductory quantum mechanics.

why: Q# and the Microsoft Quantum Development Kit are named software tools used as a course toolchain, not a general instructional element or merely a course design.
name: Q# programming language and Microsoft Quantum Development Kit
product_description: Microsoft's Q# language and Quantum Development Kit provide a programming language, compiler, simulators, debugger, and resource estimator for developing and analyzing quantum algorithms.

why: The Queered Science & Technology Center is a named UCLA research, education, and equity initiative rather than a reusable instructional element.

product_description: A UCLA research and education center that applies critical frameworks to STEM knowledge production while supporting interdisciplinary research, institutional partnerships, and representation of underrepresented STEM participants.

why: The named Quantitative Suture Assessment (QSA) is a reusable technical-skill assessment pipeline and measurement framework rather than a general instructional element.

product_description: An image- and burst-pressure-based assessment pipeline developed by Spagnulo et al. for objectively measuring surgical suturing quality and technical skill in minimally invasive surgery training.
